json.objectWhy: A neighborhood shop's one-page home on the web — a place people visit.

steps.does: Read every line of the bakery-notes and pull out the facts the page must state, each with a word-for-word quote and its page: the owner's name, the address at 14 Marlow Street by the library, opened 2019 by Ines Okafor with her brother Teo Okafor who bakes the bread, baking from 4 am, the sourdough starter kept since 2016, the opening hours (Tue–Fri 7:00 am–3:00 pm, Sat–Sun 8:00 am–2:00 pm, closed Mondays), all eight menu items with their prices, the cardamom buns selling out by 11 am on weekends, the 48 hours' notice for whole cakes and party bread, that orders are taken by phone or at the counter and not by email, and the phone number (555) 014-2290. Keep the numbers exact as written.
steps.title: Find facts

steps.does: Write index.html as one plain HTML page for Marlow Street Bakery, in the warm and simple tone the notes ask for. Header with the shop name and the line that everything is baked on site every morning. A menu section listing all eight items with the exact prices from the research. An hours section with the weekday and weekend hours and the note that Mondays are closed. An order section saying whole cakes and bread for parties need 48 hours' notice and that you call or come by the counter, with the phone number. A visit section with 14 Marlow Street and the phone number. A footer with a small line about Teo's starter, alive since 2016. No frameworks and no image files.

files.purpose: The single page: header, menu, hours, order and visit sections.

required.what: The menu with all eight items and their prices.
Opening hours for Tuesday to Friday, Saturday and Sunday, and closed Mondays.
Special orders: 48 hours' notice, call or come by the counter.
The small line about Teo's starter.

steps.title: Build page

steps.does: Write styles.css for the selectors used in index.html: cream backgrounds and dark brown text, plain and unfussy, generous spacing, menu prices easy to read at a glance, and it must still be readable on a phone screen. Use only CSS and inline SVG for any decoration — no image files, no fonts or stylesheets loaded from other sites. Write app.js as a small script that uses the weekday hours to show a plain 'Open now' or 'Closed now' line for the visitor's current day and time; nothing the page needs in order to be readable.

files.purpose: Cream and dark brown styling for the page.
Shows whether the bakery is open right now.

steps.title: Style and script

steps.does: Read the page as a critical colleague of Ines Okafor and list what is weak or missing: every price and hour against the notes, whether the hours and menu really are the first things a visitor sees, whether the tone sounds like the shop, whether the cake ordering line is clear about the 48 hours' notice, whether anything promised in the notes is missing, and whether the open/closed line can say something wrong.
steps.title: Second read

steps.does: Check the finished page by code: index.html and the other files parse, styles.css and app.js are found from the page, the required parts are present, every price and opening hour on the page matches the notes exactly, and the open/closed line cannot contradict the hours.

json.verdict: Not ready. The page is clean, semantic and well typeset, but the script that was promised is empty, nothing can be checked against the notes because the notes were not passed to me, and the first screen answers none of the three questions the goal named.

issues.text:
app.js came back empty. index.html carries a live element for the open line, `

Hours for today are listed below.

`, and styles.css defines two separate closed-state class names for it, `.hours__now.is-closed` and `.hours__now--closed`. Nothing writes to that element, so every visitor reads the placeholder sentence, which says nothing, and nobody knows which of the two class names the script was meant to set. Fix: either write app.js or delete the element and both rules. Do not ship a status line that never updates.

The notes were not given to me with the work, so I cannot check a single price or hour against them. That means these are unverified and must be confirmed before this goes out: $7.50, $8.00, $3.75, $4.25, $4.00, $4.50, $2.75, $4.75; Tuesday to Friday 7:00 am to 3:00 pm; Saturday and Sunday 8:00 am to 2:00 pm; closed Monday; the phone (555) 014-2290; 'opened the bakery in 2019'; 'kept it alive since 2016'; 'starting at 4 am'; and 'sell out by 11 am on weekends'. If any of those is not in the notes it is invented, and the number (555) 014-2290 is in the reserved fictional 555-01xx range, so a real customer cannot call it. Fix: paste the notes back to me or to the builder and check each one.

issues.about: index.html, first screen and section order
issues.text: The goal said hours and the priced menu come first. The first screen is the nav, the shop name, one lede line and the loaf drawing. No price, no hour, no open or closed. The menu starts below the fold, and hours sit third, after a dense menu with three group titles and eight price rows. On a 390 px phone you scroll past the nav, the name, the loaf, the three group headings and all eight prices before you can find out whether the shop is open today. Fix: put the open or closed line and the day's hours in or directly under the masthead, and let the menu follow immediately.

Yes, this line can say something wrong. Three ways. First, timezone: if it reads the visitor's device clock, someone looking at the page from another timezone sees the wrong open or closed answer for a shop on Marlow Street. Second, staleness: a tab left open across 3:00 pm keeps saying open unless a timer reruns it. Third, closures other than Monday, which the script cannot know. Also the status sits inside #hours, the third section down, so even a correct answer is hidden. Fix: compute against the shop's own timezone, rerun on a timer, and word it so a stale line is still partly true, for example 'Open until 3 pm'.

The planner named the bread baked on site and Teo's starter as one of the three things the page is driven by. It ended up in the footer, at 0.98rem, below the address and phone line. That is the quietest line on the page, and it is the one that makes this shop this shop. Fix: give it a place of its own above the footer, next to the loaf drawing, and let the drawing carry it.

issues.about: index.html menu heading, masthead lede and meta description
issues.text: The menu heading is 'Baked here this morning' and the description says 'Bread, pastries and coffee baked on site every morning', but the third menu group is Coffee, with filter coffee at $2.75 and an oat milk latte at $4.75, and the lede says 'Everything is baked on site every morning.' Coffee is not baked. Fix: change the heading to something the whole list fits, or move coffee under its own honest heading.

The 48 hours' notice is stated once and plainly, which is good, but the section does not say 48 hours before what, and it never says when you can call. 'Call us or come by the counter to place one' sends a reader to the counter with no hours in sight, three sections away. The phone number also appears three times on the page, in the button, in #visit and in the footer, while the address appears twice. On a 390 px phone the button becomes a full width block, so the long label 'Call (555) 014-2290 to place an order' wraps. Fix: repeat the counter hours in this section and shorten the button to the action, with the number beside it.

The address is plain text inside <address>: no map link, no second landmark beyond 'on the corner by the library', no bus, bike or parking line, and no allergen or dietary note anywhere on the page. Most people using a neighborhood bakery page are deciding whether to walk over. Also the skip link jumps to #menu, and <main> has no id, so there is no landmark to skip to. Fix: link the address to a map, say one line about getting there, and point the skip link at main content.

styles.css updated for the warmth pass: the new .masthead__welcome line gets its own size, weight and measure between the bakery name and the 4 am line, and every .menu__group is now a soft, round card (24px radius, cream surface, faint warm shadow) with the .price-list inside it set in a rounder, slightly deeper panel so the prices read as one block. issues.text: The welcome pass added a third stacked line (nav, shop name, "Welcome in. We are a small neighborhood bakery on the corner by the library.", then "Everything is baked on site every morning, starting at 4 am."), but it changed nothing about the underlying problem. The goal said the hours and the priced menu come first. On the first screen there is still no price, no hour and no open or closed line, only nav, name, two text lines and the loaf drawing. The new welcome line also reads as a subtitle under the heading, which the house rules discourage, and it repeats "small neighborhood bakery on the corner by the library" almost word for word from the meta description and repeats the landmark again in #visit. On a 390 px phone you now scroll past four text blocks, a drawing, three group headings and eight price rows before you reach the hours in the third section. Fix: cut or trade the welcome line for the two facts a visitor came for, and put the day's hours and the open or closed line in or directly under the masthead with the menu right after.

The notes were not given to me with the work, so I cannot check a single price or hour against them. That means these are unverified and must be confirmed before this goes out: $7.50, $8.00, $3.75, $4.25, $4.00, $4.50, $2.75, $4.75; Tuesday to Friday 7:00 am to 3:00 pm; Saturday and Sunday 8:00 am to 2:00 pm; closed Monday; the phone (555) 014-2290; 'opened the bakery in 2019'; 'kept it alive since 2016'; 'starting at 4 am'; and 'sell out by 11 am on weekends'. issues.about: app.js and index.html #hours, the open-now line
issues.text: app.js is no longer empty, and the part I flagged last time is fixed: it writes "Open now until 3:00 pm." or "Closed now. We open tomorrow at 7:00 am." into #open-now and reruns every minute and when the tab regains focus, so the stale-tab problem is gone. Three things remain. First, it reads the visitor's own device clock, so someone reading the page from another timezone gets the wrong answer for a shop on Marlow Street. Second, it cannot know about a closure other than Monday, so the line can still say open on a day the counter is shut. Third, styles.css defines two separate closed-state names for this element, `.hours__now.is-closed` and `.hours__now--closed`, but app.js only ever sets `is-closed`, so the second rule is dead code and the next person will not know which one is real. Also the line is buried in #hours, the third section down, so even a correct answer is hidden. Fix: compute against the shop's own timezone, word it so it stays safe on unusual days, delete the unused rule, and move the line up the page.

The second half of the warmth request made the menu worse by the house rules. Each of the three menu groups is now a 24 rem-ish radius card with a cream fill and a soft shadow (border-radius 24px, box-shadow 0 20px 32px -28px), and inside each card sits another rounded, tinted panel (.price-list, 16px radius) holding the prices. That is a card inside a card, three times over, for content that is one dense list and not three distinct objects, which is exactly what the rule against cards for everything warns about. It also fights the section's job: the menu should read as one scannable block, and it now reads as soft app cards. On a 390 px phone the three cards stack with 1.25 rem gaps and extra padding, which pushes the hours even further down. Fix: drop the per-group card and the inner panel, let the three groups stand as one aligned block with a rule between rows, and keep the rounded treatment for something that really is a distinct object.

The planner named the bread baked on site and Teo's starter as one of the three things the page is driven by. It ended up in the footer, at 0.98rem, below the address and phone line. That is the quietest line on the page, and it is the one that makes this shop this shop. Fix: give it a place of its own above the footer, next to the loaf drawing, and let the drawing carry it.
